entities.name: PMID:25091439
observations: Pooled GO-BEFORE and GO-FORWARD rheumatoid arthritis trial analysis included 1,068 participants with X-ray follow-up at weeks 52 and 104 and MRI follow-up through week 104.
Multivariable analyses reported lower structural progression with higher BMI, but retrieved evidence lacked numerical adjusted effect estimates.

entities.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
observations: Inflammatory arthritis population in the directly relevant 1–2-year BMI and imaging-progression study.

entities.name: Higher BMI
observations: BMI categories were <25, 25–30, and >30 kg/m²; higher BMI independently predicted lower probability of X-ray vdHS progression at 52 and 104 weeks.
Higher BMI independently predicted less MRI erosion-score progression over 2 years and was associated with less baseline MRI bone edema after adjustment including MRI synovitis.

entities.name: BMI and imaging progression
observations: In rheumatoid arthritis, greater BMI was directionally associated with less radiographic and MRI structural progression over 1–2 years in multivariable analyses.
The evidence is from one directly matching study; numerical adjusted odds ratios and confidence intervals were not available in the retrieved material.
